item.title: Discuz! X5.0 Race Condition + CAPTCHA-Solving Pre-Auth to RCE Chain (CVE-2026-49952)
item.description:

Tags discuz, php, forum, race-condition, captcha-bypass, ocr, account-takeover, lfi, webshell, rce, pre-auth
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System Discuz! X5.0 (PHP-based forum/CMS software)
Versions Affected Discuz! X5.0
Language / Platform PHP (target application), Python 3 (exploit tooling: requests, PyTorch/Pillow for CAPTCHA OCR)
Authentication Required No (pre-authentication chain; the exploit registers its own account as part of the attack)
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

This is a multi-stage, pre-auth-to-RCE exploit chain against Discuz! X5.0 that combines several bugs: an authcode-based DB export/import feature is abused to leak the admin’s username and MD5 password hash from a database backup; the exploit then registers a “special” crafted username containing that MD5 hash, solves the site’s login CAPTCHA using a bundled PyTorch OCR model, and wins a race condition between the DB-import process and the login flow to obtain an authenticated admin session cookie. From there it resets the admin password, logs into admincp, uploads a PHP webshell disguised as a PNG image via the header-nav icon upload feature, and abuses the plugin import/enable functionality (Local File Inclusion) to execute the disguised PHP stager, yielding an interactive webshell.

item.title: JeecgBoot mLogin Endpoint CAPTCHA Bypass Enabling Credential Brute Force (CVE-2026-8196)

Tags jeecgboot, captcha-bypass, credential-stuffing, brute-force, missing-rate-limiting, authentication-bypass
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System JeecgBoot (/sys/mLogin endpoint)
Versions Affected Not specified in source (affects instances exposing /sys/mLogin)
Language / Platform Java (Spring Boot) web application
Authentication Required No
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

JeecgBoot exposes a secondary login endpoint, /sys/mLogin, that accepts the same username/password credentials as the standard /sys/login endpoint but — unlike /sys/login — does not enforce a CAPTCHA challenge and applies no rate limiting or account lockout. This allows an attacker to bypass the CAPTCHA protection intended to slow down automated login attempts and perform efficient, unthrottled credential brute-forcing or credential-stuffing against /sys/mLogin, obtaining a valid JWT token on success.
